# Source-derived Gaussian lifetime tails

[Full proof](PROOF.md) · [Exact sources](SOURCES.json) · [Verification](VERIFICATION.md)

For the specified periodized Gaussian field in every fixed `d>=2`, on fixed
compact birth/gap ranges with the gap bounded away from zero, this candidate
derives the actual determinant-weighted estimate

    E exp(lambda (1+||f||_C4)^2) <= C.

It reconstructs the positive full-normalizer floor rather than assuming one.
Together with the [sharp axial lemma](../sharp_axial_escape_20261026/PROOF.md),
this gives `C exp(-c/r^2)` upper bounds for the essential event and, for each
fixed `q>0`, the normalized finite-lifetime q-moment above the prescribed gap.
No failure-mark convergence or selection-probability estimate is needed for
these upper bounds. Constants are not numerically evaluated.

This is an additive author-side proof. It reuses existing Gaussian-majorant
ideas and preserves posterior drift, correlations, the typed weight and the
full normalizer. Different-family scientific review remains pending. It does
not establish the broader marked-law limit or an unconditional parent theorem.

Finite algebra controls, using only Python's standard library:

```sh
python -B -S frontiers/gaussian_lifetime_exponential_tail_20261028/check_exact.py
python -B -S -O frontiers/gaussian_lifetime_exponential_tail_20261028/check_exact.py
```

These verify exact finite identities and counterexamples. The continuum
Gaussian and path-functional arguments are supplied by the proof text.

# Sharp axial escape: fewer assumptions for one lifetime moment

[Proof](PROOF.md) · [Source identities](SOURCES.json) · [Verification](VERIFICATION.md)

This additive author-side candidate establishes two bounded improvements:

- With the two exact value pins and zero derivative pins, `rH<24k` guarantees
  an axial path ending above the birth height with minimum at the lower pin.
  The old sufficient condition was `rH<=3k`. The constant 24 is sharp, and
  the strict inequality is essential.
- For a fixed lifetime power `q>0`, one uniform weighted C4-norm moment at
  an order `s>4q+3` suffices for the finite-death tail step. All-order moments
  are unnecessary for this step at a single q. An abstract counterexample
  shows why the equality case does not suffice from these bounds alone.

The deterministic result has no stochastic conjecture as a premise. Its
Gaussian application retains the actual source moment and marked-law inputs.
This does not make the parent theorem unconditional or supply independent
scientific review. No scientific status changes.

From the repository root, using only the Python standard library:

```sh
python -B -S frontiers/sharp_axial_escape_20261026/check_exact.py
python -B -S -O frontiers/sharp_axial_escape_20261026/check_exact.py
```

The outputs should be identical. Finite controls are supplemental exact
algebra checks; the continuum theorem is proved in the text.

# All directions, rare lifetimes and the critical-gap split

[Main proof](PROOF.md) · [Critical window](CRITICAL_WINDOW.md) ·
[Exact sources](SOURCES.json) · [Verification](VERIFICATION.md)

This author-side packet extends PR522/523 for the original Gaussian
regression at the two value/full-gradient pins and its full typed
determinant weight. It proves the following without a marked-law or
full-C4-support assumption.

| Regime | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Compact birth/gap ranges, gap bounded away from zero | Essential probability and finite long-lifetime probability both have matching `exp(-Theta(r^-2))` scale, uniformly over every direction. |
| `beta=k/r>=M` for a fixed sufficiently large `M` | Both probabilities have matching `exp(-Theta(beta^2))` scale. The proof retains the moment prefactors. |
| Every fixed `tau>0`, `k=tau r`, then `r->0` | Explicit contact-field formulas split essentiality from finite remote connections; each has positive limiting probability. For fixed `q>0`, `r^-3 E[X^q;finite,X>1]=Theta(r^-4q-3)`. |

The declared class is a fixed centered stationary real Gaussian field on a
fixed cubic torus in dimension `d>=2`, with even nonnegative spectrum,
strict positivity on the finite frequency cube `[-3,3]^d`, and
`sum sqrt(a_n)(1+|n|)^4<infinity`. It includes sufficiently rich band-limited
fields. Constants can depend on that fixed spectrum, dimension and torus.
Under positivity on cube four, a conditional Gaussian mesh argument also
derives Morse/distinct-critical-value genericity at each fixed pin target
and gives the conventional ordinary-H0 interpretation.

The all-direction construction uses genuine lattice Fourier modes and an
exact uniformly bounded pin right inverse. Its global maximum or separating
barrier survives a fixed zero-pin C4 ball. Gaussian translation and actual
determinant/normalizer estimates supply the lower rates. The critical-window
addition combines a fixed-neighborhood Hermite argument with off-contact
Gaussian genericity to identify the GLOBAL essential event.

The quartic cusp model, typed contact weight and local elder decision are
existing mathematics in `cusp_second_order_20261001`, and remain attributed
there. The addition is their global finite/essential split and the explicit
C4 finite-spectrum scope. Along `k=tau r`, the positive essential limit
also rules out uniform inverse-square decay, or uniform `O(r^3)` pairing
failure, across all positive gaps.

The results are conventional proof candidates with exact finite author
controls and separate same-family technical critique. Different-family
scientific review is pending. This packet supplies no status promotion,
formal-kernel result, optimal exponential coefficient or joint small-tau
asymptotic. Existing proof, workflow and status files are preserved.

Run the standard-library finite controls with:

```sh
python -B -S frontiers/all_frame_gaussian_rates_20261028/check_exact.py
python -B -S -O frontiers/all_frame_gaussian_rates_20261028/check_exact.py
```

# Completing the lifetime moment limits

[Uniform inverse moments](INVERSE_MOMENTS.md) · [Large-ratio action bridge](LARGE_RATIO.md) ·
[Exact sources](SOURCES.json) · [Verification](VERIFICATION.md)

This additive candidate closes the missing uniform-integrability step for
inverse moments of the actual finite-death failure law. It also connects
the critical-window essential event to the sharp Gaussian action.

| Result | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `P_r(F_r,0<X_r<=t) <= C r^3 t^(2/3)`, `0<t<=1` | Original periodized Gaussian; fixed dimension/torus, compact birth/gap ranges with gaps bounded away from zero, every frame, uniformly for small separation. |
| `r^-3 E[X_r^-p;F_r,finite] -> integral lambda^-p dmu_fail` for `0<p<2/3` | Each fixed parameter choice, using the existing actual marked law. Conditional moments converge after division by its positive failure mass. |
| `tau^-2 log p_E(tau;b,u) -> -I(1,u)` | The preceding C4/cube-three spectral class, fixed direction and compact births; first take the contact limit at fixed critical ratio, then let that ratio grow. |

Here `F_r` means the prescribed saddle is not the actual elder partner,
`X_r=(b-d_f(M))/(k r^3)`, and the original typed determinant weight and full
normalizer are retained. The short-lifetime proof controls all tail sectors,
including a separate scalar hard-block argument. It uses no inverse hard
eigenvalue moment or assumed independence between the field norm and Hessian.

Together with the existing positive-moment theorem [POSITIVE, Section3] and
the existing failure-mass limit, the new inverse result gives the complete
finite-valued moment convergence range for this finite-failure convention:

    r^-3 E_Pr[X_r^q;F_r,ell_r finite]
                       -> integral lambda^q dmu_fail,
    E_Pr[X_r^q | F_r,ell_r finite]
                       -> (1/a_fail) integral lambda^q dmu_fail,
                                      every real q>-2/3.

The three cases are the new inverse theorem for negative q, the known mass
limit for q=0, and the already proved positive-moment transfer for q>0.
For q<=-2/3 the prelimit finite-failure moment is infinite at each fixed
positive separation, so there is no corresponding finite-valued convergence
claim. The essential class is explicitly excluded; including its infinite
lifetime would change positive moments. The separate fourth-power endpoint
law concerns additional sequential distant-partner conditioning.

The large-ratio theorem matches the SAME constrained RKHS energy `I(1,u)`
as the fixed-positive-gap rare-event theorem. It gives an ordered bridge,
with compact-birth uniformity for the contact share, and does not exchange
the separation and critical-ratio limits.

Both arguments are conventional author-side candidates. Fresh same-family
technical checks provide error detection; different-family scientific review
remains pending. No existing proof, workflow, status or premise file changes.

```sh
python -B -S frontiers/gaussian_lifetime_limit_completion_20261029/check_exact.py
python -B -S -O frontiers/gaussian_lifetime_limit_completion_20261029/check_exact.py
```

The standard-library script checks finite algebra and source identities.
The Gaussian, geometric and limiting-measure arguments are in the proof text.
